newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Placer says banks not behind gold slip.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Placer says banks not behind gold slip.

text.p: Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc, one of the world's largest gold mining companies, said on Wednesday it did not believe central bank sales were driving down the gold price.
"I don't believe that central banks will sell gold regardless of their impact on prices," Ian Austin, chief financial officer of Placer Dome, said.
"Almost by definition, central banks are very conservative organisations," he told a news briefing.
He said that at current prices of around US$340 an ounce, gold looked like a good investment opportunity and that at some point the precious metal would recover.
Concerns among some investors that some central banks, mainly in western Europe, were active sellers of gold has helped drive gold to its lowest price in nearly four years.
"We've seem some weakness and some central bank selling, but gold markets are very resilient... Some people are just waiting for the price to bounce," Austin said.
Austin said Placer Dome took the long term view that gold will average about US$375 an ounce in mapping out its internal growth strategy.

Central banks worldwide hold an estimated 35,000 tonnes of gold, some of which is lent to institutions to support forward hedge selling programmes by mining companies, typically to finance exploration and growth.
About 30 percent of Placer Dome's gold production for the next six or seven years is forward sold at an average of US$450 an ounce, reducing in part its exposure to spot market prices, Austin said.
The company's shareholders seemed to prefer some exposure to the gold price, Austin added
